title: Control plane: implement audit-export destination model + credentials + enable/disable state machine
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Implement the control-plane data model + APIs to manage audit-export destinations for SIEM-ready audit export beta.

Scope of this ticket:
- Destination resource model supporting type=splunk|datadog|s3
- Credential storage model + secret handling (create/update/rotate) suitable for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private
- Destination state machine and transitions (enable/disable + operational states surfaced to Console)

Non-goals (for this ticket):
- Worker/queue delivery implementation (ENG-13923)
- Connector-specific send logic (ENG-13924/25/26)
- Filtering engine (ENG-13922)
- Console UI (ENG-13930)

Why:
We need a stable, secure, and operable way for customers to configure where audit events are exported, with clear state and safe credential handling. The destination model must be versionable and must support per-tenant isolation and audit logging of changes.

Notes:
- This should align with the early API sketch in Drive (audit-export-config-api-outline) but we should treat this ticket as the implementation of the finalized shape agreed in architecture/security reviews.
- Store secrets in our standard secrets backend (KMS-encrypted at rest; retrieval scoped to worker identity). Ensure no secrets returned from read endpoints.

Owners/Reviewers:
- Eng: Benji Okafor (implementation), Ethan Park (review), Priya Natarajan (sponsor)
- Security: Hanae Suzuki (secrets), Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei (export security review)
acceptance_criteria: Control plane persists an AuditExportDestination resource per workspace/tenant, with destination type and non-secret config fields.
Credentials are stored as a secret reference (never returned in plaintext from APIs); updates rotate the underlying secret.
Destination CRUD endpoints exist (create/read/list/update/delete) with validation by destination type.
State machine supports: disabled/enabled/paused/degraded; control plane enforces valid transitions and records reason fields.
RBAC: only authorized roles can create/update/delete destinations (final permission gates in ENG-13933/PR-28427, but this ticket must use the shared authz framework hooks).
All destination config changes generate audit log events (can be a stub integration if final audit wiring lands in ENG-13933).
API responses include safe health/status fields needed by Console (enabled flag, state, last_success_at/last_error_at placeholders allowed).
Migration/compatibility: schema is additive and versioned so beta iteration does not require DB rewrites.
Unit/integration tests cover validation, secret write/read paths, and state transitions.
data_model:
Proposed resource: AuditExportDestination

Partitioning:
- tenant_id/workspace_id is required and used for all queries.

Fields (non-secret):
- id (uuid)
- tenant_id
- name (customer-visible)
- type: splunk|datadog|s3
- config_json (type-specific, non-secret only)
- filter_ref (optional; owned by ENG-13922)
- enabled (bool)
- state: disabled|enabled|paused|degraded
- state_reason (string; operator/customer-actionable)
- secret_ref (opaque reference to secret store entry)
- created_at / updated_at
- created_by_actor_id / updated_by_actor_id

Per-type config notes:
- splunk: endpoint_url, hec_ack_enabled, index (optional), sourcetype (optional)
- datadog: site/intake_region, service, tags (key=value), source (optional)
- s3: bucket, prefix, region, sse_mode (SSE-S3|SSE-KMS), kms_key_arn (optional)

Important: tokens/keys are always stored in secret_ref payload; never in config_json.
credential_storage:
Credential handling requirements:
- Secrets stored using our standard secret envelope (KMS-backed encryption in Hosted/Dedicated; private deployment uses customer-managed KMS integration where available).
- Secret payloads:
  - splunk: hec_token
  - datadog: api_key
  - s3: either (a) access_key_id + secret_access_key + session_token (optional) OR (b) role_arn/assume_role (preferred for Hosted). Final selection per deployment mode documented in Private install notes.
- API behavior:
  - Create/Update accept credential fields but do not echo them back.
  - Read/List never include credentials; only include secret_ref metadata (e.g., last_rotated_at).
  - Rotate credentials supported via Update with credential block; rotation writes new secret version and swaps secret_ref pointer atomically.
- Logging:
  - Ensure request logging redacts credential fields.
  - Ensure audit log events include destination id/type and actor, but not secret material.
state_machine:
Destination lifecycle/state machine:
- disabled: destination exists but worker should not deliver
- enabled: destination configured and eligible for delivery
- paused: delivery paused due to repeated errors or operator action (beta may start with operator-only pause)
- degraded: delivery enabled but unhealthy (e.g., repeated errors, auth failures); used to surface to Console

Allowed transitions:
- disabled -> enabled (customer action)
- enabled -> disabled (customer action)
- enabled -> paused (operator action for incident mitigation; beta)
- paused -> enabled (operator action)
- enabled -> degraded (system/worker sets health; control plane stores)
- degraded -> enabled (system when healthy again OR customer after fix)
- degraded -> disabled (customer action)

Implementation approach:
- Persist current state in control plane DB.
- Provide PATCH endpoint to set enabled/disabled (customer).
- Provide internal-only endpoint for worker/SRE automation to update health-derived state and reason (degraded + reason).
api_changes:
Endpoints (names indicative; follow existing Redwood control-plane conventions):
- POST /v1/audit-export/destinations
- GET /v1/audit-export/destinations
- GET /v1/audit-export/destinations/{id}
- PATCH /v1/audit-export/destinations/{id}
- DELETE /v1/audit-export/destinations/{id}

Validation:
- type is immutable after create.
- type-specific required fields enforced (e.g., Splunk endpoint_url required).
- disallow unknown config keys (strict mode) to reduce misconfiguration.

Responses:
- include: id, name, type, config (non-secret), enabled, state, state_reason, created_at, updated_at
- include optional status placeholders for Console: last_success_at, last_error_at, last_error_code (populated by ENG-13928/worker)
open_questions: Do we allow multiple destinations per tenant in beta, or limit to N (e.g., 3) to avoid abuse? (Proposal: allow up to 5; enforce via quota config).
For Splunk: do we allow HTTP (non-TLS) endpoints in Private on-prem? (Security proposal: default deny; allow only with explicit override flag + warning).
For S3 in Hosted: do we require customer-provided IAM role (assume role) vs static keys? (Proposal: support both, but nudge role-based; Private may need static keys).
Who can set paused state in beta? (Proposal: SRE/operator only; customers can disable but not pause).
risks:
Key risks:
- Secret leakage via logs or API responses if validation/errors echo user input.
- Confusing state semantics between enabled/paused/degraded unless clearly surfaced.
- In Private deployments, secret backend capabilities vary; we need a minimal common path.
- Future schema evolution: we must keep config additive and avoid breaking validation unexpectedly in beta.

Mitigations:
- Redaction at request logging layer + explicit allowlist of response fields.
- Strict config schema per destination type and stored schema_version field.
- Add migration hooks for additive config fields and keep validation backward-compatible for existing destinations.
testing_plan:
Tests to add:
- Destination create/update validation per type (required fields, unknown fields, immutability of type)
- Secret write/read path tests using secrets backend test double
- Ensure GET endpoints never return credentials (assert payload)
- State transition tests (valid/invalid transitions)
- Multi-tenant isolation tests (cannot access destination across tenant_id)

Manual verification:
- Create Splunk destination with token; confirm token not returned.
- Disable/enable destination; confirm state updates.
- Attempt invalid config; confirm error messages are actionable and do not echo secret fields.
rollout_plan:
Rollout:
- Land behind feature flag: audit_export_beta_enabled (per-tenant allowlist)
- Enable in staging for soak testing with worker stub
- Canary: 1-2 internal tenants
- Beta: small set of design partners via Solutions Engineering

Rollback:
- Disable feature flag per tenant.
- Existing destinations remain stored but inactive when disabled; no destructive cleanup required for rollback.
